title: Consumption window allocator and burst sanity guard for Dedicated pools
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: production Dedicated pools experience short-lived microbursts that exhaust ephemeral burst credits and cause downstream latency spikes and fairness regressions. This PR adds a consumption-window based allocator plus a lightweight burst sanity guard to make per-tenant burst admission both time-aware and safety‑constrained. High level: (1) consumption-window allocator calculates per-tenant consumption over a configurable sliding window (default 60s) using an efficient EWMA sketch to avoid storing per-request history. This lets the autoscaler and admission layers reason about short-term sustained load rather than instantaneous spikes. (2) burst sanity guard enforces a soft gate that denies or delays ephemeral burst consumption when doing so would violate longer-term throughput guarantees; it prefers deferred warmup/batching instead of hard evictions. Implementation details: added pkg/autoscaler/consumption_window.go implementing the sliding-window EWMA and budget decayer; controllers/warmup_scheduler.go implements deferred warmup heuristics and a probabilistic prefill when utilization is predicted to trend up; internal/telemetry/metrics_exporter.go emits consumption_window_utilization, burst_guard_denials, warmup_prefill_attempts and burst_credit_reclaim_count. The allocator is plumbed into the admission path via controllers/admission_middleware.go and is compatible with the existing reservation ledger and burst-bank layers. Testing: unit tests for EWMA edge cases and budget roll-off (tests/autoscaler/consumption_window_test.go), integration test that simulates microburst patterns vs. sustained load (integration/dedicated/consumption_window_integration_test.go). Rollout: behind feature flag dedicated.consumption_window.enabled=false by default; staged canary to 10% of infra pools, with a 24h telemetry window and an automated rollback if burst_guard_denials > 1% and tail latency regressions exceed 5th percentile threshold. Backwards compatibility: does not change storage layout; configuration defaults preserve prior behavior. Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] metrics and dashboards added; [x] feature flagged rollout plan included. Related: complements ENG-2201 (reservoirized warm pool tuning) and addresses SUP-1456 customer incident where transient microbursts degraded throughput guarantees.

review_comments: Luca Romero: Can we lower the default window to 30s? 60s felt slow in local sims. Also please ensure the EWMA alpha is configurable.
Priya Desai: Reply: I ran sims with both 30s and 60s; 60s reduced oscillation in multi-tenant bursts. Made window configurable and exposed alpha via config with a sane default.
Ethan Park: Nit: add a short note in the admission path comment explaining why we prefer delaying vs denying in some cases.
Priya Desai: Reply: added comment and extended unit tests to cover delay path.
release_notes: Introduce consumption-window allocator and burst sanity guard behind a feature flag. Adds new telemetry metrics (consumption_window_utilization, burst_guard_denials, warmup_prefill_attempts). Default behavior unchanged until feature is enabled. Recommended canary rollout and dashboards updated.
notes_for_ops: Operators: enable feature via dedicated.consumption_window.enabled=true and tune dedicated.consumption_window.window_seconds (default 60) and dedicated.consumption_window.alpha. Watch metrics: consumption_window_utilization and burst_guard_denials. If warmup_prefill_attempts spike without corresponding utilization, revert flag for diagnostic investigation.
observability_changes: Added Grafana panel 'Ded: Consumption Window Utilization' and alert 'Ded: Burst Guard Denials > 0.5%'
test_plan: Unit tests exercise EWMA decay and budget refill; integration test runs synthetic microburst/sustained scenarios and validates that steady-state throughput meets pre-change baselines while reducing evictions during bursts.
